name: docker
description: Real Docker, inspected from the host: veth pairs and the bridge, container namespaces Docker does not register, the embedded DNS server at 127.0.0.11 (its iptables redirect, name resolution on user-defined vs default networks, and which namespace forwards upstream queries), the NAT, filter and raw rules behind port publishing, a host INPUT rule that does not protect a published port and a DOCKER-USER rule that does, loopback-only publishing and docker-proxy, egress MASQUERADE, network isolation, internal/none/host networks, a network MTU, and a subnet that collides with a corporate route

requires.docker: install Docker Engine (https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu/) and start the daemon
requires.busybox: apt-get install busybox-static (the image is built from it; nothing is pulled)
requires.go: install Go 1.24+ (the image includes the course tools)

setup: ip link add nl-dk-out type veth peer name eth0 netns nl-docker-outside && ip addr add 198.51.100.1/24 dev nl-dk-out && ip link set nl-dk-out up && ip -n nl-docker-outside addr add 198.51.100.10/24 dev eth0 && ip -n nl-docker-outside addr add 10.90.0.20/32 dev lo && ip -n nl-docker-outside link set eth0 up && ip -n nl-docker-outside link set lo up && ip -n nl-docker-outside route add default via 198.51.100.1 && ip route add 10.90.0.0/24 via 198.51.100.10

ip netns exec nl-docker-outside dnsmasq -u root --no-resolv --no-hosts --listen-address=198.51.100.10 --bind-interfaces --local=/corp.test/ --host-record=app.corp.test,198.51.100.80 --log-queries --log-facility=${EVIDENCE}/dnsmasq.log --pid-file=${EVIDENCE}/dnsmasq.pid
teardown: docker rm -f nl-dk-web nl-dk-cli nl-dk-ext nl-dk-def nl-dk-clash1 >/dev/null 2>&1; docker network rm nl-dk-app nl-dk-int nl-dk-mtu nl-dk-clash >/dev/null 2>&1; true

checks.name: the daemon: version, firewall backend, and whether the userland proxy is on
a container's eth0 is one end of a veth pair: eth0@ifN names the host-side peer, which is a port of the network's bridge
run: docker exec nl-dk-cli ip addr show eth0; i=$(docker exec nl-dk-cli cat /sys/class/net/eth0/iflink); echo "host side, ifindex $i:"; ip -o link | awk -F': ' -v i="$i" '$1==i {print $2, $3}' | cut -c1-90

checks.name: Docker's namespaces are not in `ip netns`; each container's is a file under /var/run/docker/netns, and nsenter shows the same interface from the host
run: k=$(docker inspect -f '{{.NetworkSettings.SandboxKey}}' nl-dk-cli); echo "SandboxKey: $k"; echo "in ip netns list: $(ip netns list | grep -c "$(basename $k)")"; nsenter --net="$k" ip -4 -o addr show eth0

checks.name: the bridge and its ports, and Docker's view of the network
run: ip -4 addr show nl-dk-br0 | grep inet; bridge link show master nl-dk-br0 | cut -d' ' -f2-7; docker network inspect -f '{{range .Containers}}{{.Name}} {{.IPv4Address}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}' nl-dk-app | sort

checks.name: a user-defined network: resolv.conf points at the embedded server 127.0.0.11, which forwards to the host's resolvers ("host(…)")
the default bridge: a copy of the host's resolvers, no embedded server
container names resolve on the user-defined network …
… and not on the default bridge (the query goes to the host's resolvers, which have never heard of nl-dk-web)
how 127.0.0.11 works: iptables in the CONTAINER's namespace redirect port 53 to sockets dockerd holds open inside it
run: nsenter -t $(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' nl-dk-cli) -n iptables -t nat -S DOCKER_OUTPUT; nsenter -t $(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Pid}}' nl-dk-cli) -n ss -Hlnup | sed 's/  */ /g'

checks.name: with --dns, the embedded server forwards from the CONTAINER's namespace: the query crosses the bridge from the container's address
…so the upstream server sees the host's address, after MASQUERADE — while host(…) resolvers are queried from the host's own namespace
run: grep 'app.corp.test from' ${EVIDENCE}/dnsmasq.log | head -2; docker exec nl-dk-ext grep -E '^nameserver|ExtServers' /etc/resolv.conf

checks.name: the NAT rules: DNAT for each published port (loopback-only for 18081), MASQUERADE for the network's egress
the filter path: FORWARD → DOCKER-USER (yours) → DOCKER-FORWARD; raw PREROUTING drops traffic addressed straight to a container from any other interface
run: iptables -S FORWARD; iptables -S DOCKER | grep nl-dk-br0; iptables -t raw -S PREROUTING | grep nl-dk-br0

checks.name: from outside, the published port works and the container sees the real client address
a host firewall rule in INPUT that drops port 18080 …
… does not protect it: after DNAT the packet is forwarded, never delivered to the host (this is why ufw does not cover published ports)
a DOCKER-USER rule does — matching the ORIGINAL destination port through conntrack, since the packet is already translated to :80
now the published port is blocked from outside
remove both rules
run: iptables -D INPUT -i nl-dk-out -p tcp --dport 18080 -j DROP && iptables -D DOCKER-USER -i nl-dk-out -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 18080 -j DROP

checks.name: reachable again
-p 127.0.0.1:18081:80 is reachable from the host …
… and not from outside
the host's own 127.0.0.1:18080 is served by docker-proxy, a userland process — so the container sees the bridge gateway, not 127.0.0.1
egress: a container's ping leaves the host from the host's address (MASQUERADE)
networks are isolated: the default-bridge container cannot reach nl-dk-cli's address …
… but it can reach the published port through the host, and arrives from nl-dk-app's gateway (masqueraded into that bridge)
docker network connect gives it a second interface on nl-dk-app; then names and direct traffic work
run: docker network connect nl-dk-app nl-dk-def && docker exec nl-dk-def ip -o -4 addr | awk '{print $2, $4}'; docker exec nl-dk-def ping -c 1 -W 2 nl-dk-cli

checks.name: --internal: no gateway, no default route, no MASQUERADE — nothing leaves
run: docker network create --internal --subnet 10.91.0.0/24 nl-dk-int >/dev/null && docker run --rm --network nl-dk-int course/netshell:1 sh -c 'ip route; ping -c1 -W2 198.51.100.10'

checks.name: --network none: only loopback
--network host: the host's own interfaces, including the lab's nl-dk-out
a network MTU (com.docker.network.driver.mtu) is what containers get — the fix when the host's uplink is a tunnel smaller than 1500
run: docker network create -o com.docker.network.driver.mtu=1400 --subnet 10.92.0.0/24 nl-dk-mtu >/dev/null && docker run --rm --network nl-dk-mtu course/netshell:1 ip link show eth0

checks.name: a 'corporate' network 10.90.0.0/24 is reachable from the host through the outside router
run: ip route get 10.90.0.20 | head -1; ping -c1 -W2 10.90.0.20 | tail -2

checks.name: a Docker network created with the same subnet: containers on it think 10.90.0.20 is on their own link, ARP for it on the bridge, and never reach it
run: docker network create --subnet 10.90.0.0/24 nl-dk-clash >/dev/null && docker run -d --name nl-dk-clash1 --network nl-dk-clash course/netshell:1 sleep 600 >/dev/null && docker exec nl-dk-clash1 ip route; docker exec nl-dk-clash1 ping -c1 -W2 10.90.0.20; echo "exit $?"; echo 'host:'; ip route show 10.90.0.0/24
